record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Decide whether the planarity requirement forces a worst-case lower bound on maximum degree that is strictly larger than 3 for geometric spanners. Equivalently, for every real t > 1, must there exist a planar point set P such that every plane degree-3 spanning graph on P has spanning ratio greater than t?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15. With the constraint of constructing a plane spanner, is there a lower bound on the maximum degree that is greater than 3? That is, can we show the following: For every real number t > 1, there exists a set P of points, such that every plane degree-3 spanning graph of P has spanning ratio greater than t.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. A geometric graph on P is a graph whose vertex set is P and whose edges are straight line segments between pairs of points of P, with the weight of each edge equal to the Euclidean distance between its endpoints. Such a graph is called plane if no two of its edges cross. For t ≥ 1, a geometric graph G on P is a t-spanner of P if for every pair of points p, q ∈ P the length of a shortest path between p and q in G is at most t · |pq|; the spanning ratio of G is the infimum of such t. The maximum degree of G is the largest number of edges of G incident to a single vertex.

Determine whether the planarity constraint forces a worst-case lower bound on the maximum degree that is strictly larger than 3. Equivalently, prove or disprove the following statement:

For every real number t > 1, there exists a finite point set P ⊂ ℝ² (in general position) such that every plane spanning subgraph of the complete geometric graph on P with maximum degree at most 3 has spanning ratio greater than t.

(In other words: is there a constant t > 1 and a construction that produces, for every finite point set P in general position in the plane, a plane t-spanner of P with maximum degree at most 3?)
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every finite planar point set in general position admits a plane t-spanner of maximum degree 3 with constant t (and dually, whether planarity forces a degree-3 lower bound) appears still open. Constructions of plane degree-3 spanners are known only in restricted settings: for points in convex position a plane (3+4π)/3-spanner of degree 3 is known (Biniaz–Bose et al., 2016/2017), and for general position only via the addition of a linear number of Steiner points. No subsequent work appears to have resolved the unrestricted general-position case.

status_evidence.title: Towards Plane Spanners of Degree 3
status_evidence.snippet: Plane degree-3 spanner with constant spanning ratio for points in convex position; for general position with a linear number of Steiner points.
status_evidence.claim: Constant-ratio plane degree-3 spanners are only known in special cases (convex position; general position with Steiner points), suggesting the unrestricted problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Degree 3 Plane Spanner for Points in Convex Position (CCCG 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs degree-3 plane spanner for points in convex position.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address only restricted cases, indicating the general-position version is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Bounded-Degree Plane Geometric Spanners in Practice (2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of bounded-degree plane geometric spanners.
status_evidence.claim: No claim of a constant-ratio plane degree-3 spanner for general point sets is reported.
